inspected_development_material: Trust-Hub AES, RS232, memctrl, PIC16F84, MC8051, b19, B15, and ISCAS host families
matched insertion G1, G1b, and G1c on AES, RS232, memctrl, and PIC16F84
port-aware G1c diagnostic and all RTL lexical ablation folds
research_question: Can a model rank functionally divergent Trojan variants above clean and verified benign decoys on held-out hosts and insertion mechanisms after transparent shortcut controls?
evaluation_unit: independent clean host design; variants and augmentations remain in the same group

splits.development: inspected hosts and generators may be used for design and debugging, always marked exploratory
splits.held_out_host: all variants of one independent clean host, with no source, derivative, or template leakage
splits.held_out_generator: all outputs of one independently implemented insertion generator; report overlap of trigger and payload templates
splits.final_test: requires new, previously uninspected hosts and generators; none currently exists

semantic_checks: same clean host and declared synthesis recipe for matched variants
graph and label row-order hash verification
benign decoy output equivalence for the declared input and state domain
Trojan-on output divergence with an explicit witness or bounded sequential trace
trigger reachability and no undriven trigger or payload nets
ambiguous or merged gate labels set to -1
transparent_controls: RTL tokenizer window count and length-plus-window count
directed WL histograms at fixed rounds 2 and 8
real-output XOR and output-cone equivalence rules
source language, synthesis flow, and generator-ID probes
primary_metrics: equal-host mean paired win rate with half credit for ties
fixed-threshold balanced accuracy using train-only calibration
uncertainty: host-level bootstrap is descriptive when fewer than 10 independent hosts are present; report each host and positive count

go_no_go.generator: Do not train a claimed method on a pilot if a transparent control perfectly solves its held-out hosts, if the graph view is label-blind by construction, or if semantic checks fail.
go_no_go.method: A superiority claim requires held-out-host and held-out-generator gains over the strongest legitimate control and both unimodal models, with host-level uncertainty and all failures reported.
go_no_go.real_data: Trust-Hub transfer is descriptive until independent ground truth and a prospective test are available.
go_no_go.localization: Constructed labels support synthetic localization only; real gate labels require independent validation.

claim_limits: Current four-host G1c pilot fails the generator gate because output-cone equivalence ranks every Trojan correctly.
Current Trust-Hub folds and b19 are inspected development data, not a final test.
No hardware-design reviewers are available, so engineer-usefulness and expert-validated real localization claims are excluded.
